result.reply: Sure thing — I’ll split the names, match them to your CRM contacts by email, pull in the owners, and flag any new leads as “Create contact.”

task.task: Split the full names into first and last name, check each lead against the CRM Contacts sheet by email, fill in the owner and mark new leads as 'Create contact'.
task.understanding: Split lead full names into first/last, match leads to CRM Contacts by email, pull in the Owner, and flag unmatched leads as 'Create contact'.
assumptions: Full Name contains exactly two parts (first and last); any extra spaces will be collapsed before splitting.
Email matching is case-insensitive and ignores leading/trailing spaces on both sides.
CRM Contacts sheet is the reference for existing contacts; Owner comes from that sheet.
Leads not found in CRM Contacts get status 'Create contact'; matched leads get 'matched'.
No Zetaris tables are needed; all reference data is in the uploaded file's CRM Contacts sheet.

spec.name: lead_split_and_crm_match
spec.summary: Split lead full names, match to CRM Contacts by email, fill Owner, and flag new leads for contact creation.

advisories: step 3 (lookup): 12 of 25 'Email' values match the reference; the rest get the not_found status

checks.detail: same output on a second run

checks.detail: renaming 'Lead ID' raised: ValueError: Missing column: Lead ID

advisories.detail: evaluate_condition deviates from spec: for eq/ne it returns False when row value is non-string (e.g., number, None) instead of using text() conversion; contains and starts_with swap the row value and condition value (spec: text(v).strip().casefold() in text(value).casefold(), code does opposite).
split step treats non-string Full Name (e.g., numeric Lead ID) as non-blank and attempts to split, producing unexpected First/Last Name; blank() only returns True for None or empty string.
flag step is hardcoded to a single condition and does not implement generic 'match': 'all'/'any' logic over a condition list, making future extensions error-prone.
clean_text step ignores the 'case' parameter (lower/upper/title) defined in the step config; only 'none' is handled, reducing maintainability if the automation is updated.

memo.rationale: The automation correctly splits lead names, matches emails against CRM Contacts (12 of 25 matched), pulls Owner for matched leads, and flags unmatched leads as 'Create contact'. QA passed all 34 test cases (100% pass rate) producing 25 output rows. However, QA advisories reveal non-blocking defects: evaluate_condition deviates from spec for eq/ne and contains/starts_with; split step mishandles non-string Full Name values; flag step is hardcoded; clean_text ignores the case parameter. The critic notes that 13 leads will be flagged for contact creation, which requires human verification. These issues are fixable but warrant human review before production deployment.
risks: evaluate_condition bug: eq/ne returns False for non-string row values instead of applying text() conversion; contains and starts_with swap row value and condition value — could cause incorrect matching
split step treats non-string Full Name (e.g., numeric Lead ID) as non-blank and attempts to split, producing unexpected First/Last Name values
flag step hardcoded to a single condition, not generic 'match': 'all'/'any' logic — future extensions error-prone
clean_text ignores the 'case' parameter (lower/upper/title); only 'none' handled, reducing maintainability
Only 12 of 25 leads match CRM Contacts; 13 will be flagged 'Create contact' — human must verify these are genuinely new leads
Assumption that Full Name contains exactly two parts may not hold for all leads (e.g., middle names, suffixes)
what_you_get: 25 output rows with columns: First Name, Last Name, Email, Owner, Status
12 rows with Owner populated from CRM Contacts and Status = 'matched'
13 rows with empty Owner and Status = 'Create contact' for human follow-up
Name splitting applied to all leads (subject to the split-step caveat above)
